competitions.name: AlpacaEval
competitions.tagline: An automatic evaluator for instruction-following language models.
competitions.description: AlpacaEval is a fast, cheap, and highly reliable automatic evaluation pipeline for chat LLMs. It measures model win rates against a reference baseline using LLM-based judges, achieving a 0.98 Spearman correlation with ChatBot Arena.

participation.howToSubmit: Fork the repository, add your model config under src/alpaca_eval/models_configs/<model_name>, run evaluate_from_model to generate outputs and score, and open a PR with the config, outputs, and updated leaderboard.
participation.submissionFormat: Model configuration YAML, model outputs JSON, and updated leaderboard CSV.
participation.computeDetails: Submitters generate their own model outputs (locally or via API) and run the evaluation judge using their own OpenAI/Anthropic API keys.
participation.verification: Community submissions are self-reported. Top-5 models can be verified by core maintainers who run the decoding and evaluation themselves.

competitions.quickstart:
pip install alpaca-eval
export OPENAI_API_KEY=<your_api_key>
alpaca_eval --model_outputs 'example/outputs.json'

competitions.name: ClawProBench
competitions.tagline: Trace-aware evaluation of AI agents with runtime coverage and frozen workplace-style holdouts.
competitions.description: ClawProBench evaluates model capabilities inside the OpenClaw runtime across 102 active scenarios. It uses deterministic grading and structured reports to measure agent performance. The benchmark supports multi-trial runs and ranks models using a custom FinalScore metric.

participation.howToSubmit: To run ClawProBench, submit results, or discuss model evaluation for the leaderboard, contact: xyh920691910@outlook.com.

participation.computeDetails: Live runs expect a working local openclaw CLI plus the auth and config required by the surfaces exercised by the selected scenarios.
participation.verification: Deterministic grading with custom checkers and order-insensitive matchers.

competitions.name: Skoltech Anomaly Benchmark
competitions.tagline: Evaluate outlier and changepoint detection algorithms on multivariate time series from a physical testbed.

competitions.name: Mathematics Distillation Challenge — Equational Theories — Stage 2
competitions.tagline: Generate machine-verifiable Lean 4 proofs or countermodels for equational implications over magmas.
competitions.description: A competition based on Terence Tao's Equational Theories Project. Participants submit a Python solver that must output machine-verifiable Lean 4 certificates (proofs or countermodels) for equational implications. Submissions are evaluated deterministically by a Lean judge across Solo and Marathon tracks.

participation.howToSubmit: Submit a single Python file named `solver.py` (up to 500 KB) implementing the Solo or Marathon I/O protocol.
participation.submissionFormat: A single `solver.py` file that outputs JSON verdicts ('true' with Lean 4 proof, or 'false' with countermodel).
participation.computeDetails: The solver runs in a sandboxed environment (up to 2 CPUs, 2GB RAM). LLM calls are mediated by the organizer's proxy to external APIs (e.g., GPT-OSS-120B on DeepInfra).
participation.verification: Deterministic Lean 4 judge verifying the generated proofs or countermodels.

amber compile scenario.json5 --docker-compose amber-out
cp amber-out/env.example amber-out/.env
AMBER_CONFIG_CODING_AGENT__MODEL_NAME=gpt-4o AMBER_CONFIG_CODING_AGENT__OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-xxx docker compose -f amber-out/compose.yaml --env-file amber-out/.env up
